newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to legislate against copper wire theft.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to legislate against copper wire theft.

text.p: The South African government is considering legislative controls on trade in copper wire in a bid to cut telephone cable thefts, Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo said on Tuesday.
The country's telephone service, already battling to meet a 1.8 million backlog in telephone installations, is plagued by copper wire thefts.
Naidoo said he expected that the phased transition to fibre-optic cable would cut down on vandalism and theft.
Direct losses of copper cable totalled around 30 million rand ($6.6 million) in the last financial year.
The state telecommunication utility Telkom said last month the scale of thievery had become a national problem, causing major service disruptions.
Even fibre-optic cable -- which has no blackmarket value -- is being ripped up by thieves looking for the $1.50 per kilo (2.2 pounds) that copper will bring, but who don't know the difference.
Pressure for action has mounted as business groups lose patience with sudden cuts in service inflicted by cable theft, which can leave a company phoneless for weeks in some cases.
